title: Staff Vacancies
metaDescription: Current teaching and support staff vacancies at Rosehill College, Papakura. See open roles, requirements and how to apply to join our team.

sections.heading: Join our team at Rosehill College
sections.lede: Explore exciting career opportunities at Rosehill College, where we are committed to fostering a dynamic and supportive environment for both students and staff. Whether you are passionate about teaching, administration, or support roles, we invite you to be a part of our vibrant educational community and contribute to the success and growth of our students.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.html:
The terms and conditions, including base salary, for teaching positions are set by the Secondary Teachers' Collective Agreement. The base salary for trained and registered teachers will range from $61,329 to $103,086 (rates effective from 2 December 2024), depending on the applicant's qualifications and experience. An individual's actual base salary will be established by a salary assessment once a role is confirmed.

A Rosehill College Application Form must accompany your CV and cover letter:

  • Application Form — Teachers
  • Application Form — Relief Teachers
  • Application Form — Support Staff

sections.heading: Current vacancies
sections.html:
#### Kaihautū te Tari Māori 3 MU + 1 MMA — Full Time

‍He ngaakau maahaki taau moo Te Reo Maaori me oona Tikanga? He tangata matatau koe ki te koorero, aarahi me whakaako i Te Reo Maaori.  E rapu ana maatou i teetahi Kaihautuu Maaori hei whakaako i aa maatou aakonga mai te Tau 9 ki te Tau 13. Ki te mahi tahi me te whakahaere i eetahi atu kaiako e rua, i roto i te tari Maaori. Kia whakahaere i ngaa poowhiri o te kura. He kaiako koe e matatau ana i ngaa Taumata Maatauranga aa-motu (NCEA) i Te Reo Maaori tae mai te reanga iwa ki te taumata tuatoru. Ko te tumanako, ka whakauu tonu te tuuranga nei ki te tuuhono atu ki te mana whenua, araa too maatou hapuu o Ngaati Tamaoho. Ko te tumanako, ka whakatinanahia ngaa whakarerekeetanga i roto i te tari Maaori a teeraa tau, kia haangai ki Te Maataiaho maatauranga. Mehemea kei a koe ngaa puukenga katoa, teenaa tono mai.

Do you have a passion for Māori Language and its culture? Are you someone who is able to speak fluently, guide and teach in Te Reo Māori. 

We are looking for a Head of Faculty Māori to teach our year 9 - 13 students. To work alongside and manage two other teachers within the department. To run pōwhiri as required. You are a teacher that has strong grounding in NCEA levels 1-3 with its associated requirements, and the relevant clarifications of the standards for the academic success of our students. An ability to be able to make connections with our local Hapū of Ngāti Tamaoho is also desired. There is an expectation that changes be implemented within the Māori Department next year to align with the National Curriculum Refresh. 

<hr>

#### Student Support Facilitator — Full Time

We are currently seeking a committed and enthusiastic facilitator to help run our Puāwai student programme. This is a full time role working with a small group of students to help them engage in the classroom. The successful candidate will understand the importance of integrating our school values into this classroom space.

<hr>

#### Head of Faculty English (4MU) — Full Time, **Start date: Term 1, 2027 or by negotiation**

‍We are seeking a well-organised, innovative and inspiring leader for our growing English team. The successful candidate will be able to improve student achievement in both English and Literacy, with a focus on wellbeing and positive learning relationships. 

Applicants should have a current New Zealand teacher registration and a strong knowledge of Phase 4 of the New Zealand curriculum for English. Experience in leadership is an advantage. The successful candidate will have:

* knowledge of the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi
* a genuine passion for English teaching
* experience in building and shaping an effective team
* demonstrated capacity to improve student achievement
* relational practices that tautoko positive relationships within our kura and ensure te reo me ōna Tikanga are upheld
* a genuine interest in collaborative planning for the implementation of Phase 5 of the New Zealand Curriculum
* experience with differentiated teaching and UDL for English and Literacy skills development
* a clear understanding of NCEA English
* experience in teaching and programme development for both junior and senior levels of English
* commitment to mana ōrite mō te mātauranga māori, and cultural responsiveness is also essential.

**Applicants must have NZ working rights.**
